the stack structure dependence on the magnetic properties of PtMn/Co/Ni thin films is investigated.

the stack structure dependence on magnetic properties is investigated for thin films that consist an antiferromagetic PtMn and ferromagnetic CoNimultilayer for field free spin-orbit torque induced magnetization switching devices, and that the improvement in the current-induced magnetization switch characteristics compared with the previous work is confirmed by using patterned Hall-cross devices.
the magnetic properties can be tuned by changing the stack structure and that the stack structure optimization improves current-induced magnetization reversal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stack structure dependence on the magnetic properties of the thin films and their application to spin-orbit torque switching devices.
the stack structure dependence on the magnetic properties of the PtMn/[Ni/Co] films for spin-orbit torque switching device.
the magnetic properties of thin films for field-free spin orbit torque-induced magnetization reversal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stack structure dependence can be utilized to improve the magnetic properties of the PtMn/[Ni/Co] films, and hence the switching properties of the devices.

PtMn/[Ni/Co] films with a stack of 3.0 nm PtMn, 1.5 nm Ni, 0.6 nm Co, and 0.5 nm Pt exhibit a large effective anisotropy, high saturation magnetization, and a large exchange bias field, and thus are promising for field-free spin orbit torque switching devices.
the magnetic parameters are strongly dependent on the stack structure, and the current-induced magnetization reversal can be improved by engineering the stack structure of the PtMn/Co/Ni films.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a stack structure of PtMn/(Co/Ni) _{2} /Pt is the most suitable structure to achieve a high switching current density of 1.5 MA/cm ^{2} and a low switching current pulse of 0.3 ns.
a PtMn/Co _{2} Ni _{2} /PtMn/Co/CoNi stack with an interfacial perpendicular magnetic anisotropy of 0.8 mJ/m ^{2} is suitable for spin-orbit torque switching devices.
a proper stack structure of PtMn/Co/Ni is important to achieve the best performance of the spin-orbit torque switching devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stack structure dependence on magnetic parameters should be considered when designing the spin-orbit torque switching devices.

the stack structure of the PtMn/Co/Ni film plays a critical role in the magnetic parameters of the Co/Ni layer, and the magnetic parameters are tunable by controlling the thickness and the composition of the Co/Nicore/shell multilayers.
the stack structure dependence on magnetic properties is a crucial factor to be considered when designing spin-orbit torque switching devices.
